title: THIS_AND_FUTURE Start-Time Shift Realigns Inherited UNTIL, EXDATE, and RDATE by Wall-Clock Delta

citations.verbatim_quote: When the given recurrence instance is rescheduled, all subsequent instances are also rescheduled by the same time difference. For instance, if the given recurrence instance is rescheduled to start 2 hours later, then all subsequent instances are also rescheduled 2 hours later.

The UNTIL rule part defines a DATE or DATE-TIME value that bounds the recurrence rule in an inclusive manner.  If the value specified by UNTIL is synchronized with the specified recurrence, this DATE or DATE-TIME becomes the last instance of the recurrence.

The final recurrence set is generated by gathering all of the start DATE-TIME values generated by any of the specified "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, and then excluding any start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties.

rationale: RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 states that when a recurrence instance is rescheduled with `RANGE=THISANDFUTURE`, all subsequent instances are rescheduled by the same time difference (e.g., 2 hours later). When a calendar store materializes `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edits as a split (R-L3-001) or an in-place first-instance update (R-L3-002), copying an inherited `RRULE`'s `UNTIL` bound, future `EXDATE` entries, and future `RDATE` entries verbatim without applying that same wall-clock shift produces two user-visible anomalies: (1) if `dtstart` moves to a later time of day while `UNTIL` was synchronized to the old start time on the final day (RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10), the final occurrence now falls after `UNTIL` and is silently clipped; and (2) future occurrences previously deleted via `EXDATE` no longer match the shifted occurrence timestamps (RFC 5545 Section 3.8.5.1), resurrected on the timeline while future `RDATE`s remain at the old time. By `STORE_POLICY`, whenever a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit shifts `dtstart` within the same temporal class without supplying an explicit `rrule`, inherited `UNTIL`, unpatched future `EXDATE`s (excluding dual `EXDATE`s belonging to pre-split overrides), and unpatched future `RDATE`s shift by the same wall-clock delta.
store_implication: When `edit` is invoked with `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range (at either a non-first instance creating a new-UID segment per R-L3-001 or the first instance updating the main component in place per R-L3-002), `dtstart` is present in the patch, `rrule` is not in the patch, and the patched `dtstart` has the same temporal class (`DATE`, floating `DATE-TIME`, or timezone-aware `DATE-TIME`) as the targeted split occurrence: (1) compute `wall_delta = naive(new_dtstart) - naive(split_occurrence_dtstart)`; (2) if the inherited `rrule` contains an `UNTIL` part and `wall_delta != 0`, shift `UNTIL` by `wall_delta` in the series' local wall-clock coordinates (converting back to `UTC` when `DTSTART` is `UTC` or `TZID`); (3) strip any `LEGACY_DUAL_EXDATE` entries belonging to pre-split standalone overrides before shifting, then shift remaining unpatched future `exdate` and `rdate` entries by `wall_delta` in local wall-clock time; and (4) prune any `exdate` entry that is not a candidate of the updated recurrence set.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Daily `America/New_York` series at `09:00 EDT` (`13:00Z`) bounded by `UNTIL=20250508T130000Z` with a deleted occurrence `EXDATE=2025-05-07T09:00:00-04:00[America/New_York]`: editing `2025-05-06T09:00:00` (`THIS_AND_FUTURE`) to `dtstart='2025-05-06T11:00:00-04:00[America/New_York]'` (`wall_delta = +2h`) shifts the new segment's `UNTIL` to `20250508T150000Z` (retaining May 8 at `11:00`) and shifts `EXDATE` to `2025-05-07T11:00:00-04:00[America/New_York]` (keeping May 7 deleted).
If the caller explicitly supplies a new `rrule` in the `THIS_AND_FUTURE` patch, the caller's `rrule` (and any `UNTIL` inside it) is used verbatim without automatic shifting.

First-instance `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit (`recurrence_id == master.dtstart`, normalized per R-L3-002): shifting `dtstart` from `09:00` to `11:00` applies the exact same `+2h` wall-clock shift to inherited `UNTIL`, `EXDATE`, and `RDATE` as a non-first-instance split.

scenarios.name: edit_this_and_future_start_shift_realigns_until_exdate_and_rdate
scenarios.description: Splitting an America/New_York series at May 6 with THIS_AND_FUTURE and moving dtstart from 09:00 to 11:00 shifts inherited UNTIL (+2h in wall-clock time so May 8 is not clipped), future EXDATE (keeping May 7 excluded), and future RDATE (moving May 10 to 11:00).

scenarios.name: edit_first_instance_this_and_future_start_shift_realigns_until_and_exdate
scenarios.description: Editing the first instance of an UNTIL-bounded series with THIS_AND_FUTURE range and shifting dtstart by +2 hours updates the series in place and shifts both UNTIL and EXDATE by +2 hours.

audit_notes: Added explicit STORE_POLICY rule and scenarios for THIS_AND_FUTURE wall-clock realignment of inherited UNTIL, EXDATE, and RDATE when dtstart shifts without an explicit rrule.
Verified citations in rfc5545.txt Sections 3.8.4.4 (L6434-L6439), 3.3.10 (L2295-L2299), and 3.8.5.1 (L6748-L6751).
